title: AWS Security, Networking & Cost Governance
exp: Enterprise cloud interviews cover VPC Endpoints, IAM Role Assumption, KMS Envelope Encryption, and AWS Cost Anomaly Detection.
pts: **VPC Interface Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)** vs **Gateway Endpoints (S3 / DynamoDB)**: routing traffic over AWS internal network without Internet Gateways.
**IAM Security:** `sts:AssumeRole`, cross-account access, Session Tags, Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations.
**KMS Envelope Encryption:** Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) generated locally, encrypted by KMS Customer Managed Key (CMK).
**Cost Control & Governance:** AWS Budgets, Cost Anomaly Detection, S3 Lifecycle Rules (Intelligent-Tiering to Glacier Deep Archive).
pr: Write a cross-account IAM role trust policy

r: Deep mechanics of AWS Security, Networking & Cost Governance under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.
Use profiling tools to measure actual baseline allocation before optimizing.
Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.
Favor simple, well-tested modular architectures over premature complexity.

qa.q: What is the difference between VPC Gateway Endpoints and Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink)?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Gateway Endpoints are free VPC route table entries used strictly for S3 and DynamoDB. Interface Endpoints use Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) with private IP addresses powered by PrivateLink to securely connect to other AWS services or custom SaaS applications, billed per hour + data processed.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: Explain how Envelope Encryption works in AWS KMS.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** KMS generates a plaintext Data Encryption Key (DEK) and an encrypted DEK. The application encrypts payload data locally using the plaintext DEK, discards the plaintext DEK from memory, and stores the encrypted DEK alongside the payload.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Boxing allocates a System.Object header (16 bytes on x64) on the managed heap and copies the value type bytes into it. Span<T> is a ref struct allocated strictly on the execution stack, providing contiguous memory access without heap allocation or array copying.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Boxing inside a high-throughput loop generates thousands of ephemeral Gen 0 objects, triggering frequent GC pauses and thread pool delays. Fix: use generic collection interfaces (IList<T>) and Span<T>/Memory<T> for byte slicing.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Span<T> provides zero-allocation performance, but ref struct rules forbid storing it on the heap, as class fields, or across async await points (where Memory<T> must be used).
